_doc: Episode 0 endings (docs/GDD.md section 6). Week.ending_id(choice) picks one from the last choice on the 999 steps (week 13, 7 July) + route, bond, self, flags (memory_2016, sayo_found, letter_101, makabe_letter_sent, makoto_apologised) and rival fates. pages = shown in order, then the title + the week summary + end card. family_epilogue is added when Makoto apologised (week 10) and the ending isn't a dark one.
end_card:
EPISODE 0 - NEKOTSUKI - END
Enma's Ledger has written it all down. The next episode will remember.
family_epilogue: In August a man in a Tokyo suit climbs the 999 steps for the first time in twenty-five years. He stops at the top, takes off his glasses, and says a woman's name to the empty shrine. The bell on the offering box rings once, very softly. He sits on the step until the lanterns go out, and for once he does not run.

okaeri.title: Okaeri - Welcome home
pages: You climb. Nine hundred and ninety-nine steps, and then one more that has never been there for anyone who wasn't meant to stand on it. Your foot finds it. The lanterns below go silent all at once, like a town holding its breath.

Amane is at the top, exactly where a white-and-black cat waited for twenty-two years. He is not crying. He is waiting, the way only he knows how.

You say it. Not because a ghost said it first in 1890. Because you mean it, tonight, in this life.

"Tadaima."

The bell on his collar rings once - the longest, clearest note anyone in Suzunari has ever heard.

"...Okaeri, Senpai."

A debt of a thousand needles is paid. His cat ears are gone in the morning. So is the rain. What the two of you are to each other from now on is yours to decide - and for the first time, nobody else is deciding it for you.

red_thread.title: The Red Thread
pages: At the top of the steps the old shrine bell hangs from its frayed rope. Amane looks at it, then at you, and holds out the end of the rope like a question.

You ring it together. The sound rolls down the 999 steps and out over the river and the shopping street and the sea. Every cat in Suzunari - on walls, on roofs, in windows - sits down and turns to face the shrine.

The faint red line around your little finger glows, just for a second, and then it is simply there, like it always was. Tied. Not a debt any more. A choice, made twice.

He holds your hand all the way down. It takes a very long time. Neither of you minds.

this_life_love.title: This Life
pages: You ask him for the bell. He understands before you finish the sentence. His hands shake on the red cord - and then he unties it himself, and puts it in your palm.

Something leaves him. You see it go: three hundred years of waiting, a cat on a staircase, a hundred letters he never heard. His eyes go wide and empty and very young.

"Senpai...?" He looks at you as if for the first time. A long pause. Then, slowly, a small new smile that belongs to nobody but him. "...Hi. I think I like you. Is that weird? We just met."

He doesn't remember anything. He chose you anyway.

The bell goes back to the shrine, where it can finally be quiet. In Enma's Ledger, under Nekomori Amane, the past-life column is blank - and the present one is full.

this_life_stranger.title: This Life (a stranger)
pages: The cord comes undone. The bell is warm in your hand. Amane blinks at the shrine, at the lanterns, at you.
"Sorry," he says politely, the way you'd speak to a stranger on a staircase. "Do I... know you?" He bows, and walks down the 999 steps on his own, and doesn't look back.

Weeks later you see him at the school gate laughing with two first-years from his class. He is fine. He is better than fine. He walks past you like the rain walks past a closed window.

It stops raining in Suzunari that July. You are not sure that's a happy ending. Neither is the bell.

cat_who_waits.title: The Cat Who Waits
pages: You don't climb. You catch the last train instead, the one that plays Toryanse at the crossing. Going is easy. Coming back is the frightening part.
Years pass in Tokyo. You get a job, an apartment, an umbrella you never need, because it never rains on you.

In Suzunari it rains every day. Every Tanabata a boy - then a young man - in a black hood sits on the 999th step until the lanterns go out, waiting for someone he can't stop remembering.

The town calls him the cat who waits. He doesn't mind the name. He only minds the waiting.

endless_festival.title: The Endless Festival
pages: You take his hand and step onto the thousandth stair together, at the dusk hour, on purpose. The world turns red. The rain falls upward. The festival on the other side never ends.

In Ura-Suzunari the lanterns are always lit and the takoyaki is always hot and nobody ever has to go home. Amane laughs more than you have ever heard him laugh. Rin grumbles from his collar that this is the laziest ending she has seen in three hundred years.

In the real Suzunari two students are listed as missing. The rain stops the same night. Every Tanabata, if you stand on the 999th step and hold your breath, you can hear festival music from very far away - and two people laughing.

hidden.title: Kamikakushi - Hidden
pages: You step onto the thousandth stair alone, the way you did when you were seven. Nobody runs after you this time.
Ura-Suzunari takes you gently. The red sky, the upward rain, the festival. You forget your name somewhere near the station that doesn't exist. Then you forget that you forgot.

Amane searches the steps every evening for a year. Mio films the dusk every day and finds, on one tape, a boy in a school blazer counting stairs and never reaching the top.

The Ledger lists Asagiri Toru under 'hidden'. The next episode will have to come and find him.

homecoming.title: Homecoming
pages: You don't go up for yourself. With Letter 101 in your pocket and Amane's hand in yours, you walk into the red dusk to the dry riverbed where the children build their little towers of stones.

She is there, a woman in a faded summer kimono, helping a small ghost balance one more stone. She looks up. She sees her son - fifteen, not one - and drops every stone she is holding.

"Amane?"

Rin reads Letter 101 aloud, all of it, in her rude old voice that cracks on the last line. It was never about debts. It was about coming home.

Three people walk down the 999 steps in the morning. The town will spend a year arguing about what that means. Episode 8 begins exactly here.

god_returned.title: The God Returns to the Shrine
pages: You do what Shirasagi Kyoko asked. You walk him to the empty shrine and stand aside, and the bell on his collar is lifted onto the offering stand where it sat for a hundred years.
The shrine doors close. Behind them, something that was a boy is a god again, and a god does not cry, and a god does not wait for anybody.

Suzunari's luck comes back overnight. The shops reopen, the maneki-neko factory hires again, the Shirasagi ships come home full. It never rains again.

You never see him again either. Sometimes, at the dusk hour, the bell in the closed shrine rings once, by itself, when you walk past.

dog_and_cat.title: The Dog and the Cat
pages: Inukai Takeshi climbs the 999 steps with a lantern and a length of sacred rope, his son beside him. "The old way," the priest says. "Dogs guard the road. Cats keep what they shouldn't."

The rope goes around the cat shrine three times. Hayate stands in front of you with his bad ankle and his arms out, the way a white dog once stood in front of a ghost on a long road. Amane does not fight. He just looks at you until the seal closes.

The rain stops. The two-tailed cat is never seen again. Hayate walks you home every evening for the rest of high school and never once lets you walk alone.

On quiet nights you still hear a small bell from the hill. The priest says it's the wind. Hayate doesn't say anything.

right_distance.title: Just the Right Distance
pages: You walk down the steps beside him. Not ahead, not behind. When he reaches for your sleeve you let him hold it for the last ten steps, and then he lets go on his own.

In September he joins the photography club with Hina. In October he argues with Reiji at a council meeting and wins. In November Mio teaches him a ghost story and he tells it better than she does.

You are not together. You are something with a different, quieter name, and he is the one who chose it.

On New Year's Day you climb the steps to pray. His cat ears pop out the moment he sees you - just for a second, just on that day.

"Happy new year, Senpai," he says, perfectly steady. It doesn't rain.

unsent_letter.title: The Letter That Was Never Sent
pages: At the foot of the steps, Makabe-sensei is waiting with an envelope he wrote in 2001 and finally sent. "Not you, Asagiri," he says. "This one's mine to walk."
He climbs the thousandth stair in his school cardigan, holding the letter, the way he should have climbed after her twenty-five years ago. The dusk closes behind him.

In the morning a woman walks down the 999 steps holding an opened letter and crying the ordinary way, with no rain at all. Makabe-sensei does not come down.

On his desk in the staff room, every letter he ever kept is neatly tied with red string. Episode 4 begins with them.

two_of_us.title: Just the Two of Us
pages: Nobody else comes to the festival. Hayate is in the hospital, or the hospital says he never existed. Hina's newspaper has blank pages. Mio's camera films only rain. The president's chair in the council room is empty.

Amane is waiting at the top of the steps with two cups of festival lemonade. "Everyone's busy tonight," he says brightly. His smile does not reach his eyes. "So it's just us. Isn't that nice, Senpai? Isn't that what we wanted?"

The town is very quiet after that. The cats watch from every wall. Somewhere, very far down in Enma's Ledger, a column of names is crossed out in a small, neat, two-tailed hand.

This is the worst ending. You can find your way back from it in the next life. Probably.

remembers._doc: Week.remembered(ending): after the ending pages, up to `max` lines about choices the town remembers. Each line needs all `flags`, none of `none`, not one of `not_endings`; `who` (a rival's full name) skips it when that person is hidden or in two_of_us. Highest p first, then file order.
remembers.title: WHAT SUZUNARI REMEMBERS

lines.t: You took one of Amane's festival tickets. He kept the other half, folded very small, in his phone case.
You went to the festival with Hina. Her photos of that night are the best she ever took, and she knows it.
You all went to the festival together. Somewhere there is a photo where everyone is blinking.
You promised to bring Sayo home, and you did. Chiyo-san sets a third cup at dinner now.
You promised to bring Sayo home. The riverbed on the other side is still waiting for you to keep it.
You still dream of festival sugar. One bite of you never came back down the steps.
You never ate on the other side. Whatever else happened, all of you came home.
You hugged Dad at the station. He held on longer than you did.
"It wasn't watching you, Dad. It was waiting for me." He believed you. That surprised you both.
Dad climbed the 999 steps beside you without a word. His knees complained for a week.
Dad visits Grandpa's grave now. He brings the old shogi pieces and loses on purpose.
You asked Dad to come back for Tanabata. He bought the ticket. He never said whether he used it.
Dad told you why he hates this town. He hates it a little less since.
Dad knows you remember 2016. You talk about it on the phone, sometimes, late.
Dad told you about someone he left on the steps, twenty-five years ago. He still can't say her name.
On the first night you asked why Dad never brought you back. By July you knew, and so did he.
Grandpa's dream-hint about Dad was the truest thing anyone told you all spring.
Hayate's relay medal hangs at the dog shrine. He says half of it is yours.
You promised Hayate you'd take him next time. He holds you to it, every time.
Nobody ever admitted who put your name down for the relay. Sato Yui smiles when you ask.
Hina published. For one week, the whole town read the Suzunari Shimbun.
Hina waited, like you asked. Her story is still in a drawer, finished, waiting for the right day.
Hina wrote the real story of the curse. Nobody believed it. Everybody read it.
Hina never did find out who runs the Ura board. She has a wall of red string about it.
Sato Yui still runs the Ura board. The posts have been kinder since you found her.
Gataro brought the six Jizo up from the river. Mio dressed each one in a new red bib.
You promised Mio you'd find the six Jizo together. You kept looking after spring ended.
"Whatever you chose, I'm still here." Reiji remembers saying it exactly. So do you.
Reiji trusts you more than his own family. He told the council so, in writing.
Reiji stopped calling the Shirasagi luck "luck". He calls it bookkeeping.
Reiji reopened the harbour file. Someone has written a question mark after "accident".
Reiji still keeps the nurse's list in his council folder, every name checked twice.
Tomi-san still has the list of names and dates. She hasn't had to add one since you took the page.
You told Shirasagi Kyoko you'd think about it. She sent a thank-you card anyway. You didn't open it.
The heron company that bought the shuttered shops has an empty office in Tokyo. You checked.
"Amane isn't Sayo." Makabe-sensei says it to himself on bad days. It helps.
Makabe-sensei never told the class about the rainy night. He told you, and that was enough.
You read one of Makabe's letters. You never told him which line stayed with you.
One of Makabe's letters is still in your desk. It was never yours to send.
Makabe-sensei goes to the river on Sundays. When you see him there, you nod.
Aunt Haruka still sets out a second cup when it rains. "For the boy who cries," she says, and won't explain.
Aunt Haruka put Dad's old school photo on the fridge. The girl laughing beside him is Sayo.
You knew the next line of Haruka's lullaby without ever being taught it. She cried, then made dinner.
Aunt Haruka believes in past lives now. She won't say since when.
The 2016 negative is in your drawer. Held up to the light, there are two children on the steps.
The old umbrella you took home opens by itself whenever it rains. You don't mind.
You watched the lantern on the 13th night from your window. You still see it when you close your eyes.
You woke Chiyo-san on the hill. She insists she was only resting her eyes.
Chiyo-san knew about the nails all along. She was only waiting for someone to ask.
You stood guard on the last nights. Whatever came, it didn't come through you.
You asked if a bell can be made to forgive. Rin rang once, which might mean yes.
You know the girl's name now: Aya. Somebody in this town has to keep saying it.
Every 13th night a light burns late in the Shirasagi house. You notice it now.
Grandpa told you someone would fall. When they did, you were ready.
Grandpa's warning about Reiji's mother made sense in the end. Most of his warnings did.
Grandpa told you about the hundred letters. In the end you counted them yourself.
